title: 5 Huntingdonshire planning applications that you should know about
content: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Planning committees across Huntingdonshire are busy as ever, with plenty of applications and appeals coming through. We've compiled a list of just some of the applications that are currently pending or have been approved in our areas. Here are some that might have gone under the radar. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home." title: New eight-home development in Warboys approved despite resident objections
content: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans for a new eight-home development in Warboys have been approved despite objections from residents and the parish council. The proposal, from applicants Mr and Mrs Robinson, involves constructing eight detached homes on land between Heath Farm and Heath Pond, north of Heath Road in Warboys. The land is currently classed as agricultural. Plans include three three-bedroom and five four-bedroom homes, 16 parking spaces, landscaping and a footpath linking the site to the village. It was granted Permission in Principle in July 2025 for between four and nine homes, establishing that the site could be developed for housing. The plans include three-bedroom and four-bedroom homes, 16 parking spaces and landscaping (Image: Huntingdonshire Planning Portal) Despite the formal submission of these plans, the proposal has faced objections from Warboys Parish Council and residents.
